info.title: Ignition HTTP API
info.description:
### About this page
This specification covers all public HTTP API endpoints for the Ignition platform and currently
installed modules. It is intended to be used by developers to understand the capabilities and
data formats used by the API. This documentation is generated from the
[OpenAPI](https://www.openapis.org/) specification document which is available in JSON format
[here](/openapi.json).

get.description: Returns a list of the available deployment modes

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of items to skip before returning results.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
The name of a field to sort by. Use `asc(fieldName)` or `desc(fieldName)`
to specify the sort direction as ascending or descending, respectively.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: A search string to filter items by. Terms separated by whitespace.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter items by field name, using format like `fieldName[op]=value` where `op` is one of: `eq` (equals), `ne` (not equals), `cn` (contains), `sw` (starts with), `ew` (ends with), `gt` (greater than), `gte` (greater than or equal), `lt` (less than), `lte` (less than or equal), `rgx` (regular expression).

title.description: A short title for the mode.

description.description: A few sentences describing the purpose of the mode.

resourceCount.description: Number of resources defined in this mode

total.description: The total number of items available

matching.description: The number of items matching the filter and/or search criteria

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, as specified in the query parameter

offset.description: The number of items to skip before starting to return items, as specified in the query parameter

changes.description: List of changed resources, with new signatures

problem.description: If the operation failed, this field will be populated with the exception that was thrown.

references.description: If the operation would impact other resources, this field will be populated with the paths of those resources. The operation will not be performed until the client confirms the operation by sending a request with the same parameters, including the confirm field set to true.

connectionResetParams.description: A set of commands (one per line) that will be executed each time a connection is pulled from the pool. Can be used to reset environment variables.

defaultTransactionLevel.description: The isolation level to use for each connection.

poolInitSize.description: The initial number of connections that are created when the pool is started.

poolMaxActive.description: The maximum number of active connections that can be allocated from this pool at the same time, or negative for no limit.

poolMaxIdle.description: The maximum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being released, or negative for no limit.

poolMinIdle.description: The minimum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being created, or zero to create none.

poolMaxWait.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait (when there are no available connections) for a connection to be returned before throwing an exception, or -1 to wait indefinitely.

validationQuery.description: A SQL query that will be used to validate connections from the pool. This query MUST be an SQL SELECT statement that returns at least one row.

testOnBorrow.description: When true, connections will be validated before being borrowed from the pool. If the connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool, and we will attempt to borrow another.

testOnReturn.description: When true, connections will be validated before being returned to the pool.

testWhileIdle.description: When true, connections will be validated by the idle connection evictor. If a connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool.

evictionRate.description: The number of milliseconds to sleep between runs of the idle connection evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle connection evictor thread will be run.

evictionTests.description: The number of connections to examine during each run of the idle object evictor thread (if any).

evictionTime.description: The minimum amount of time in milliseconds a connection may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any).

failoverProfile.description: Another datasource that will be used to handle queries if this datasource faults.

failoverMode.description: <dl><dt>STANDARD</dt><dd>Standard failover mode means that this datasource will fail over when a connection cannot be retrieved, but when connectivity is restored, connections will again come from this datasource.</dd><dt>STICKY</dt><dd>Sticky failover mode means that once this datasource fails over, connections will continue coming from the failover datasource until the failover datasource itself fails or the Gateway is restarted.</dd></dl>

slowQueryLogThreshold.description: Queries that take longer than this amount of time, in milliseconds, will be logged. This helps to find queries that are not performing well.

validationSleepTime.description: The time in milliseconds between database validation checks.

connectionResetParams.description: A set of commands (one per line) that will be executed each time a connection is pulled from the pool. Can be used to reset environment variables.

defaultTransactionLevel.description: The isolation level to use for each connection.

poolInitSize.description: The initial number of connections that are created when the pool is started.

poolMaxActive.description: The maximum number of active connections that can be allocated from this pool at the same time, or negative for no limit.

poolMaxIdle.description: The maximum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being released, or negative for no limit.

poolMinIdle.description: The minimum number of connections that can remain idle in the pool, without extra ones being created, or zero to create none.

poolMaxWait.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait (when there are no available connections) for a connection to be returned before throwing an exception, or -1 to wait indefinitely.

validationQuery.description: A SQL query that will be used to validate connections from the pool. This query MUST be an SQL SELECT statement that returns at least one row.

testOnBorrow.description: When true, connections will be validated before being borrowed from the pool. If the connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool, and we will attempt to borrow another.

testOnReturn.description: When true, connections will be validated before being returned to the pool.

testWhileIdle.description: When true, connections will be validated by the idle connection evictor. If a connection fails to validate, it will be dropped from the pool.

evictionRate.description: The number of milliseconds to sleep between runs of the idle connection evictor thread. When non-positive, no idle connection evictor thread will be run.

evictionTests.description: The number of connections to examine during each run of the idle object evictor thread (if any).

evictionTime.description: The minimum amount of time in milliseconds a connection may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the idle object evictor (if any).

failoverProfile.description: Another datasource that will be used to handle queries if this datasource faults.

failoverMode.description: <dl><dt>STANDARD</dt><dd>Standard failover mode means that this datasource will fail over when a connection cannot be retrieved, but when connectivity is restored, connections will again come from this datasource.</dd><dt>STICKY</dt><dd>Sticky failover mode means that once this datasource fails over, connections will continue coming from the failover datasource until the failover datasource itself fails or the Gateway is restarted.</dd></dl>

slowQueryLogThreshold.description: Queries that take longer than this amount of time, in milliseconds, will be logged. This helps to find queries that are not performing well.

validationSleepTime.description: The time in milliseconds between database validation checks.

Prevents changes from being applied to the configuration system for a limited time. Time may be specified
in the request body. While this lock is held, any other changes will be queued (block) until the
lock is released. While locked, it is safe to make external changes to the filesystem.
The next call to `POST /data/api/v1/scan/config` will release the lock.

requestBody.description: Contains lock options, such as the time to hold lock before timing out.

acquireTimeout.description: Time (in seconds) to wait before successfully acquiring the lock. Default: 10

holdTimeout.description: Time (in seconds) to hold the lock before timing out. Default: 60

400.description: Bad request body - unable to parse timeout option

408.description: Unable to acquire lock within timeout

actor.description: The user who acquired the lock
